what_its_for: Doxercalciferol is a form of vitamin D used to treat secondary hyperparathyroidism, which means your parathyroid glands are overactive. This commonly happens in people with chronic kidney disease (CKD) who are on dialysis or not yet on dialysis. It helps lower the levels of parathyroid hormone (PTH) in your blood to keep your bones and minerals balanced.
how_to_take: Doxercalciferol comes as a capsule to take by mouth or as an injection given through your IV during dialysis. If you are taking the capsule, swallow it whole with water. You can take it with or without food. If you receive it as an injection, a healthcare provider will give it to you at your dialysis center. Always take it exactly as your doctor tells you.
dosing: Your doctor will decide the right dose for you based on your PTH levels and lab results. For capsules, the usual starting dose is 1 mcg per day if you are not on dialysis, or 10 mcg three times per week at dialysis if you are on dialysis. Your doctor may adjust your dose every 8 weeks based on your blood test results. Never change your dose without talking to your doctor first.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose of the capsule, take it as soon as you remember the same day. If it is already the next day, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one. If you miss your injection at dialysis, your healthcare team will handle it — just let them know.
storage: Store doxercalciferol capsules at room temperature, between 59°F and 77°F (15°C and 25°C). Keep them away from light, heat, and moisture. Do not store them in the bathroom. Keep this medication out of reach of children and pets. Dispose of unused or expired capsules safely — ask your pharmacist about a medicine take-back program.
what_to_avoid: Avoid taking extra vitamin D supplements, calcium supplements, or antacids that contain magnesium unless your doctor approves. These can raise your calcium or other mineral levels too high. Avoid eating large amounts of calcium-rich foods (like dairy products) without checking with your doctor. Tell your doctor about all other medications, vitamins, and supplements you take, as some can interact with doxercalciferol.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away if you notice signs of too much calcium (hypercalcemia), such as: nausea, vomiting, constipation, loss of appetite, extreme thirst, frequent urination, confusion, muscle weakness, or bone pain. Also call if you feel unusually tired, have irregular heartbeat, or notice swelling. Go to the emergency room or call 911 if you have a seizure or lose consciousness. Do not stop taking this medication without talking to your doctor first.
when_it_works: Doxercalciferol starts working within a few days, but it may take several weeks before your PTH levels reach the target range. Your doctor will check your blood levels regularly (usually every 2 to 4 weeks at first) to see how well it is working and to adjust your dose if needed. You may not feel different right away, but the medication is still doing important work inside your body.
special_populations: Kidney Disease: This medication is specifically made for people with kidney disease, so it is generally safe to use in this group when monitored carefully. Elderly Patients: Older adults may be more sensitive to vitamin D and calcium changes, so close monitoring is important. Pregnancy and Breastfeeding: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. Doxercalciferol may not be safe during pregnancy or breastfeeding, and your doctor will weigh the risks and benefits. Children: Safety and dosing in children have not been well established — talk to your child's doctor for guidance.
